model.name: Learning Activity / Course Delivery
model.purpose: Represent one governed delivery aggregate for a bounded learning activity, course, class, cohort, self-paced offering, workshop or session, connecting immutable learning intent to actual instruction, participation evidence, assessment and bounded outcomes.
model.scope_statement: Owns delivery identity and lineage, mandatory delivery profile, exact course, activity, curriculum and objective bindings, delivery-scoped design, provider and role assignments, cohort and participation assertions, schedule, location and modality, resource and tool bindings, instruction, attendance and learning-event assertions, assessment administrations, progress and completion assertions, quality, lifecycle, interoperability, access and retention. Person, Learner, Organization, Programme, Course or Activity Definition, Competency, Academic Session, Location, Resource, Tool, Enrollment, Attendance, Assessment Definition, Submission, Assessment Result, Qualification, Credential, Dataset, Communication, Artifact and Audit masters remain external.
in_scope: Delivery identity, profile, lineage, provider, authority, curriculum, objectives, instructional design, roles, cohorts, enrollment bindings and access
Schedule, sessions, modality, locations, resources, tools, assignments, instruction, facilitation, attendance, participation and learning-experience events
Assessment administrations, result links, feedback, progress, mastery and completion assertions, quality, lifecycle, interoperability, privacy, retention and safe agents
out_of_scope: Independent person, learner, provider, programme, course or activity definition, competency, session, location, resource, tool, enrollment, attendance, assessment, submission, result, qualification, credential, communication, artifact or audit master lifecycles
Inferring enrollment from access, attendance from login, learning from activity completion, mastery from one score, qualification from course completion or causality from learning analytics
Implementing a student information system, learning management system, learning record store, assessment platform, content repository, credential wallet or universal education policy and legal regime

boundary_notes.neighbor: Course, Activity, Curriculum or Programme Definition
boundary_notes.distinction: Reusable intent, structure, prerequisites and objectives are external versioned definitions. The delivery binds exact revisions and records one governed realization.
The delivery owns source-qualified participation and role assertions. External identity and enrollment masters retain admission authority, lifecycle and learner rights.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Session, Attendance or Learning Experience Event
boundary_notes.distinction: These are planned or observed occurrences within the delivery. Source events keep their own actor, action, object, context, time, authority and voiding semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Assessment Definition, Submission, Result or Grade
boundary_notes.distinction: The delivery binds assessment revisions and issues delivery-scoped administration and grading assertions while external evidence and result masters retain identity and review history.

Completion or mastery can support a separately authorized achievement, credit, qualification or credential. The delivery cannot issue or own those records unless explicitly delegated by their master system.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint stable IDs for delivery roots, releases, profile bindings, schedules, role and participation assertions, session and learning events, assessment administrations, progress and completion assertions, reviews and lifecycle events. Preserve authoritative external course, learner, enrollment, assessment, result, qualification and credential identities; never use title, class code, date or digest as delivery identity.
registry_links: Dimension-local learning, curriculum, delivery, participant, assessment, outcome and policy registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative source plus delivery identifier, mandatory delivery profile and lineage head, not by course title, class code, dates, instructor or digest.
Keep reusable definition, planned activity, actual session, access, attendance, experience event, assessment, grade, mastery, completion, qualification and credential as distinct assertion classes.
patch_rules: Extensions declare education sector and delivery profile, target finding, semantics, authority, lifecycle, accessibility, privacy, assessment, quality and interoperability effects.
Released rosters, schedules, events, submissions, results, grades and outcomes are immutable; corrections create attributable successors and repeat deliveries create new roots.
A patch must never silently change curriculum revision, objectives, eligibility, learner identity, accommodations, grading rule, source evidence or original event history.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when delivery identity, profile, curriculum binding, roles, participants, schedule, evidence, assessment, outcomes, lifecycle and provenance remain intact.
ISCED, ELM, Edu-API, OneRoster, Caliper, CASE, QTI, xAPI, CLR, Common Cartridge and CourseInstance mappings pin versions and declare omissions, semantic conflicts and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system delivery or class-offering identifier qualified by source and delivery profile.
Governed globally resolvable delivery IRI under a controlled namespace.
Dimension UUID when no authoritative or governed global identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate planned, effective, event, submission, assessment, result, release, ingestion and knowledge times and preserve source precision.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {delivery-id}--{release-or-session}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use title, class code, date, timestamp or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, delivery and release binding, source and profile versions, definition, resource, assessment and grading revisions, generating actor or tool, event and knowledge times, access marking and provenance.

policies: A Learning Activity or Course Delivery is not the reusable Course or Activity Definition, Curriculum or Programme, a Learner, Enrollment, Session, learning event, Assessment, Qualification or Credential.
Access, login, attendance, participation, engagement, learning, assessment success, mastery, completion, credit, qualification and credential remain separate source-qualified assertions.

Delivery ownership does not transfer ownership of person, learner, organization, programme, course, activity, competency, session, location, resource, tool, enrollment, attendance, assessment, submission, result, qualification, credential, communication, artifact or audit masters. Delivery disposition never cascades to linked masters.

Agents may validate, link and project allowlisted data, but enrollment admission, learner contact, accommodation decisions, grading, mastery or completion signoff, credential issuance, protected disclosure and disposition require delegated authority and applicable policies.

read: Resolve Dimension policies, delivery identity and lineage, profile, definition bindings, objectives, roles, participants, schedule, resources, instruction, events, assessments, progress, outcomes, provenance and access purpose.
create: Record delivery identity and profile, exact course or activity definition, objectives, provider, roles, schedule, resource and policy bindings before accepting participants or events.
update: Append enrollment, access, schedule, resource, session, participation, instruction, submission, result, grade, progress, completion, review, correction, cancellation or supersession events with actor, authority, rationale, event and knowledge time and expected revision; never overwrite released history.
delete: Apply learner-rights, academic, contract, privacy, records, retention and legal-hold policy; cancel or archive a delivery separately from deleting eligible working copies, preserve required evidence lineage and minimum tombstone, and never cascade deletion to linked masters.

access.default_rule: Deny direct learner identifiers, demographics, disability or accommodation details, communications, submissions, grades, behavioural analytics, predictions and protected content unless a purpose-bound Dimension policy permits the minimum necessary view. audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, delivery, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, release or affected fields, source revision and outcome without copying protected learner data unnecessarily.

checklist.notes: Delivery, release, profile, schedule, role, participant, event, assessment, result, outcome and lifecycle identities are distinct.
Formal, non-formal, informal and workplace profiles and definition, programme, learner-record and event boundaries are explicit.
Curriculum binding, objectives, roles, participants, schedule, resources, instruction, evidence, assessment, progress and completion are first-class.
Attendance, activity, assessment and outcome observations retain source method, scope, time, confidence and limitations.
Register, bind, assign, enroll, schedule, deliver, record, assess, evaluate, review, project and retain are governed.

People, learners, programmes, courses, activities, competencies, sessions, resources, enrollments, assessments, results, qualifications and credentials remain external masters. Proposed relations or mapping versions remain held for review.
Planning, publication, enrollment, scheduling, activation, pause, closure, completion, cancellation, correction, repeat and archive preserve history.
Definition, curriculum, role, enrollment, schedule, activity, evidence, assessment, outcome and crosswalk links are typed.
Planned, effective, session, event, submission, assessment, result, release, ingestion and knowledge times remain distinct.
Physical, virtual and blended locations, rooms, platforms and event contexts remain source-qualified.
Plans, agents, used resources, generated events, submissions, results, outcomes, revisions and invalidations preserve provenance.
Provider, curriculum, instruction, enrollment, assessment, support, accessibility, privacy, data and records duties are separated.
Identity, revision, eligibility, schedule, resource, accessibility, evidence, grading, outcome and stale-head checks are explicit.
Purpose-bound views, learner privacy, accommodations, protected evidence and field-redacted projections are explicit.
Cancellation or archive, working-copy deletion, retained evidence, holds and minimum tombstones are distinguished.

ISCED, ELM, Edu-API, OneRoster, Caliper, CASE, QTI, xAPI, CLR, Common Cartridge and CourseInstance mappings are versioned and loss-aware. Proposed relations or mapping versions remain held for review.

known_omissions: No successful independent Claude or Grok result was available; education-sector, pedagogy, accessibility, learner-rights, analytics, regional and legal review is required before canonical promotion.
The slash name covers several delivery forms through a mandatory profile. Formal course, cohort, self-paced, workplace, community, informal and single-activity profiles require their own invariants.

No approved relation rows were supplied. The registry parent link to Personal Education or Qualification and proposed definition, learner, enrollment, assessment, result and credential relations remain holds.
Edu-API remains Candidate Final Public and its full specification is access-controlled. Common Cartridge 1.4 is Candidate Final. No final-version conformance claim is made for either.
OneRoster is K-12 oriented, Edu-API is higher-education oriented, ELM is European, and CLR, Caliper, QTI, CASE and xAPI cover narrower exchange domains.
Accessibility, child protection, consent, grading, record access, retention, intellectual property and credential authority vary by jurisdiction, provider and learning context.
conflicts: Course, class, section, offering, learning opportunity, activity, session and delivery are used differently across standards. The mandatory profile and source mapping preserve those distinctions.
Login, access, attendance, participation, engagement, learning, mastery, completion, credit, qualification and credential can disagree and must not be collapsed.
Learner analytics, personalization, privacy, accessibility, safeguarding, academic integrity, transparency and instructor autonomy can impose competing requirements.
regional_assumptions: K-12, higher education, vocational, workplace, professional, community and informal learning have different provider authority, learner-rights, accessibility, safeguarding and records rules.
ISCED is a statistical classification, ELM is European, OneRoster is K-12 oriented and Edu-API targets higher education; none supplies a universal delivery lifecycle.
QTI, CASE, Caliper, xAPI, CLR and Common Cartridge are exchange profiles whose adoption and conformance requirements do not automatically govern the Vercy aggregate.
adversarial_checks: Reject a delivery without stable identity, mandatory profile, exact definition and objective revisions, provider authority, schedule basis and lifecycle head.
Reject enrollment inferred from access, attendance from login, engagement or learning from time online, mastery from one score, qualification from completion or causality from analytics correlation.
Reject a repeat delivery or correction that overwrites earlier rosters, schedules, events, submissions, grades, feedback, outcomes or source evidence.
Reject copied learner, enrollment, resource, assessment, submission, result, qualification or credential masters whose independent identity, authority and lifecycle are lost.

Reject agent enrollment, accommodation, grading, progression, credential issuance, protected disclosure or disposition outside delegated authority and applicable learner-rights, accessibility, privacy and retention controls.
